summary: Edvard Westermarck worked in philosophy and religious studies. After studying at the University of Helsinki (~1881–1890), he held posts at the London School of Economics (~1904–1929) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918–1932).

Edward Albert Gait was an Indology and history scholar who studied at University College London (~1880–1882). He founded the Bihar and Orissa Research Society in 1914 and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Charterhouse School, Merton College, and Oxford, later serving as Professor at East India Company College (1845) and at the Foreign Office (~1860–1863).

Edward Byles Cowell studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian studies, he served as Principal of Sanskrit College (1858–1864) and Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge and Christ's College (1867–1903).

Edward C. Dimock Jr. worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics, earning degrees from Yale and Harvard. He was assistant professor at the University of Chicago (1966–1993) and president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972–1986).

Edward Capps was a history and linguistics scholar. He studied at Illinois College, Yale, Berlin, Munich, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held faculty posts at Illinois College (1887–1888), Yale University (1890–1907), and Princeton University (1907–1936).

Edward Clive Bayley worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College and the East India Company College (~1840–1842), entering the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

Edward Conze studied at Tübingen, Heidelberg, Kiel, Cologne under Max Scheler, and under Max Walleser. Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held appointments at the University of London, Wisconsin-Madison, Washington, Berkeley, and Lancaster University.

Edward Delavan Perry was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Columbia University and the University of Tübingen. He served as Jay Professor of Greek and Latin at Columbia University from 1891 to 1931.

Edward Denison Ross studied at UCL and under Theodor Nöldeke at Strasbourg. Active in Iranian studies, linguistics, and Tibetology, he held posts at UCL, Aliah University, the National Archives of India, and served as Director of SOAS (1916–1937).

Edward Elbridge Salisbury studied at Yale and in Europe under Burnouf, Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Bopp, and Lassen. An Indologist and linguist, he taught at Yale (1841–1854) and was president of the American Oriental Society (1873–1880).

Edward Evan Evans-Pritchard studied at Exeter College, Oxford, and the London School of Economics. A scholar of religious studies and other fields, he held posts at LSE, Cairo University, Cambridge, and served as professor at Oxford (1946–1970).
Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is an Indology, Buddhist, and religious studies scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Roderick S. Bucknell. He held an academic post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett works in linguistics and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at UCLA under Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, and studied with Anna Szabolcsi, later holding research posts at UCLA (1996–2000) and the University of Virginia (2000–2001).

Edward Granville Browne studied at Newcastle, Pembroke College, Cambridge, and under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell. Specializing in Iranian studies and linguistics, he served at Cambridge as lecturer in Persian (1888) and Adams Professor of Arabic (1902).

Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Harvard. He taught at UC Berkeley in Oriental Languages (~1947–1984) and served as president of the American Oriental Society (1975–1976).

Edward Hamilton Johnston studied at Eton, New College, and Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1909–1924) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (~1937–1942).

Edward James Rapson studied at Hereford Cathedral School and St John's College, Cambridge. An Indologist, linguist, and historian, he worked at the British Museum (1887–1906) and was Professor of Sanskrit at UCL (1903) and Cambridge (1906–1936).

Edward Joseph Thomas studied at St Andrews under John Burnet and at Emmanuel College, Cambridge. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at Cambridge University Library (~1909–1939) and served as Cambridge's Oriental Languages Department dean.

Edward Kamens is a specialist in Japanology and Buddhist studies who completed his education at Yale University (~1970–1982). He pursued his academic career there from ~1986, becoming Sumitomo Professor Emeritus of East Asian Languages & Literatures.
